  "text": "Martin found his father in the greenhouse, washing flowerpots in a bucket.

“The van’s here,” Martin said.

His father turned a pot upside down. Water dripped onto his slippers.

“These aren’t going.”

“Then you don’t need to wash them.”

“They’ll stack better clean.”

Beyond the glass, two men carried the kitchen table down the path. One walked backwards, watching his feet.

“Have they got the extra leaf?” his father asked.

“It’s underneath. I showed them.”

His father rubbed at a white mark on the rim.

“Your mother used to put that in for Christmas.”

“I know.”

“Even when there were only four.”

Martin lifted an empty sack from the bench. Beneath it was a tomato, small and split along one side.

“Do you want this?”

“Not that one.”

His father pointed towards the door, where a single plant leaned against its string. Three green tomatoes hung close together.

“They won’t ripen now,” Martin said.

“On a windowsill they will.”

“There’s a windowsill at the flat.”

“I’ve seen it.”

Martin put down the sack.

From the house came the scrape of something heavy, followed by an apology neither man could make out.

His father dried his hands on his trousers.

“Have you got a box?”

“For the pots?”

“For those.”

Martin found a shallow tray beneath the bench. He twisted each tomato free and laid it inside.

His father took the split one too.

“That’ll do in a sandwich.”

They stood aside while the men brought out the last chair. Then Martin carried the tray to the car."
